headline: Growth accelerates, but a one-time gain distorts profit
summary_short: Revenue rose to $119.8B (+24.2% y/y), led by Google Cloud (+82% y/y, including newly-started TPU-system revenue) and Google Services (+15% y/y); operating income grew 30.4% y/y to $40.8B. Net income surged to $112.2B, driven almost entirely by a $99.0B non-operating gain on equity securities, not operating performance.
summary_long: Revenue reached $119.8B (+24.2% y/y, +9.0% q/q), led by Google Services (+15% y/y: Search & other +$9.1B, YouTube ads +$1.3B) and Google Cloud (+82% y/y, aided by newly-started TPU-system revenue recognition). Operating income grew 30.4% y/y to $40.8B; margin slipped 2.1ppt q/q to 34.0% as G&A absorbed a $1.5B charge tied to a Stockholm court's PriceRunner (Klarna) antitrust ruling. Net income of $112.2B and diluted EPS of $9.11 were driven almost entirely by OI&E swinging to $98.0B, including a $99.0B gain on equity securities (SpaceX and a private company), not operations. Cash rose to $55.9B and equity to $640.5B after a $49.6B equity/preferred capital raise; no share repurchases occurred; quarterly capex was $44.9B.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by Google Services +$12.0B (+15% y/y, incl. Search & other +$9.1B, YouTube ads +$1.3B) and Google Cloud +$11.1B (+82% y/y), aided by newly-started TPU-system revenue recognition.

30% y/y growth driven by revenue growth across Google Services and Google Cloud, partially offset by higher cost of revenues (depreciation, TAC, infrastructure) and operating expenses (compensation, advertising, depreciation).

Q/q compression reflects a $1.3B q/q rise in G&A that included a $1.5B charge for a Stockholm Patent and Market Court antitrust ruling favoring PriceRunner (a Klarna subsidiary); margin is still up y/y.
Cost of revenue rose $6.9B y/y on higher depreciation, inventory/other costs, content-acquisition costs, and technical-infrastructure operations costs, edging ahead of revenue growth this quarter.

Surge is almost entirely non-operating: OI&E rose to $98.0B from $2.7B a year ago, primarily a $99.0B net gain on equity securities attributed by the filing to unrealized gains in the SpaceX and a private-company holding.
